subparts.stem: For what values of $x$ will the series converge?
subparts.solution: The series will converge if $|\text{common ratio}| < 1 \implies |x - 2| < 1 \implies -1 < x - 2 < 1 \implies 1 < x < 3$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: An infinite geometric series converges if and only if its common ratio $r$ satisfies $|r| < 1$.
step_by_step: Expand the absolute value inequality: $-1 < x - 2 < 1$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting the lower bound and only solving $x - 2 < 1$.

subparts.stem: Evaluate the sum of the series when $x = \sqrt{5}$.

mark_breakdown.desc: Substituting x = sqrt(5) to obtain 12 / (3 - sqrt(5)) approx 15.7

subparts.solution: $\sum_{k=1}^\infty 12(x - 2)^{k-1} = \frac{12}{1 - (x - 2)} = \frac{12}{3 - x}$. And $x = \sqrt{5}$ satisfies $1 < x < 3$. Therefore, when $x = \sqrt{5}$, the sum of the series is $\frac{12}{3 - \sqrt{5}} \approx 15.7$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: When $|r| < 1$, the sum is given by $S = \frac{u_1}{1 - r}$. Check that the given $x$ satisfies the convergence condition from part a before evaluating.
step_by_step: Find the sum formula in terms of $x$: $S = \frac{12}{1 - (x - 2)} = \frac{12}{3 - x}$.
